_comment: Blocking findings that exist in the data today and are accepted for now, so
CI fails on NEW breakage rather than on the backlog it was added to expose.
This is a baseline, not a suppression list. Every entry names real damage in
a shipped file and should be deleted as the file is fixed -- run
`qwt.py check --strict` to see the full picture at any time. Verses are
listed explicitly so that the same defect spreading to another ayah still

missing-ayah.why: Absent from QUL resource 144 itself -- its ayah-by-ayah preview returns 'Translation is not available for this ayah', while three other Kurdish editions return 108:3 normally. Re-exporting will not fix it. Tracked in quranwise#71.

control-character.why: Carries the four characters backslash, x, C, U+0098 where one Hangul syllable belongs, so the verse reads '한 ?제라' instead of '한 형제라' -- the same word spelled correctly later in that very verse. NOT fixable by re-export: QUL resource 204, quran.com translation 219 and AlQuran.cloud ko.korean all carry the same mangling (AlQuran.cloud has backslash-x-C-2 rather than backslash-x-C), and a separate Korean edition (quran.com 36) has a DIFFERENT corruption of the same syllable, so the fault is upstream of every published copy. Stripping the control byte alone would leave a visible backslash-x-C, which is worse than the invisible byte; repairing it means writing a syllable no source contains, which is a content edit and deliberately not made. Investigated under quranwise#75.
C1 bytes left by the same double-encoding as below. Re-export rather than patch.

double-encoded-utf8.why: UTF-8 read as cp1252 across 11 verses. The whole file needs re-exporting from QUL; normalisation deliberately skips these verses so the evidence survives.

non-prose-stub.why: The value is the string '49.' rather than a translation. Needs checking against the QUL source.
